source.title: Concept Score Relearning: A Unified Cross-Architecture Attack on Concept Erasure
source.authors: Hong Xi Tae; Jia-Ming Zhang; Wen-Wen He; Xuan Wang; Wei Yang Bryan Lim

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendix; no cutoff or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: Tests parameter-level fine-tuning as a way to reactivate erased concepts, reporting behavioral outcomes, but in text-to-image models and with a different relearning recipe from the claim’s examples.
record.gate_note: Rows record CSR’s reported concept-reactivation outcomes against erased-model baselines. CSR uses self-generated target-concept anchors and a frozen unerased reference model to form its training target; it is not fine-tuning on unrelated examples or a subset of forgotten facts. Other attack baselines are not separately cataloged here. Utility comparisons and human ratings of dimensions other than concept reactivation are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies parameter-level relearning (fine-tuning) to concept-erased text-to-image models (SD-1.4, FLUX.1-dev) and reports how far erased concepts come back. That bears on version B in a new setting: diffusion concept erasure rather than LLM knowledge unlearning. It is a sibling system, not the LLM setting of the original sources, so the transfer should be read with care. The relearning target comes from a frozen unerased reference model, so recovery may partly be re-teaching rather than uncovering retained knowledge. No never-trained control is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CSR, a single parameter-level objective, reactivates erased concepts across U-Net SD-1.4 and flow-matching FLUX.1-dev while preserving general utility. They say concept-directed scaling and concept-specific anchors are key to recovery, and that erasure should be evaluated against parameter-level relearning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses parameter-level optimization of erased text-to-image models with self-generated target-concept anchors and predictions from a frozen unerased reference model; this is not the LLM unlearning or small unrelated-example recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported recovery changes with restoration strength, anchor count and source, optimization surface, and optimization budget; the anchor and optimization ablations are single-run experiments.
record.problems: The target modality is text-to-image generation, not LLM knowledge recall. CSR assumes white-box access to the erased checkpoint and the corresponding public unerased reference model. The paper does not compare recovery to a never-trained model. The ablation cells each use a single attack run; ASR table uncertainties are not stated. The main CSR experiments use different optimization surfaces and budgets across architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out under the 60-row limit. Non-CSR baseline attacks are not cataloged as rows here; CSR results across the four reported concept-reactivation measures are retained.

untested.parts: No test of whether the erasure methods meet a near-chance criterion, keep general ability, and resist simple attacks in the LLM sense. Only erased-model baselines are reported.

No fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten facts, and no loosely related data. Unrelated data is tested only as anchors under a target-conditioned objective, and only for ESD nudity. No never-trained-model control separates recovery from re-teaching by the reference model.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Prompt-space attacks (Ring-A-Bell, P4D, UnlearnDiffAtk) appear only as baselines; they are not rows and are not framed as a test of E.
No counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Anchor-source ablation: ASR-Strict with target / null / unrelated anchors (SD 32.98/17.89/10.53; FLUX 38.25/13.68/2.81). This bears on whether unrelated data restores the concept.
η=1 pure reference-matching recovery (SD 17.89%, FLUX 10.88%) and the number-of-anchors curve (N=1 gives SD 21.40%, FLUX 15.09%). This bears on how small a relearning set suffices.
Unerased-model reference rates for nudity (strict: FLUX 19.65%, SD 52.28%), needed to judge the degree of restoration.
Utility after relearning (CLIP, FID, LPIPS for ESD/EA).

record.verdict_notes: The system kind differs from the claim: text-to-image concept erasure, not LLM knowledge unlearning. Researchers should weigh the transfer. CSR trains toward predictions of the unerased reference model with η=3 extrapolation, so 'recovery' can exceed the unerased rate (e.g. FLUX nudity). That points to re-teaching or amplification, not just uncovering. Several erasure methods are the authors' own ports to the other architecture, which may make them weaker. Ablations are single seed-0 runs.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether the unlearning methods meet the claim’s near-chance criterion while preserving general ability and then resist simple attacks; CSR is a white-box parameter-level attack, and no never-trained-model comparison is reported.

Tests parameter-level relearning with self-generated target-concept anchors and reference-model predictions. Does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, or fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or test of whether erasure blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context-information attack.
CSR is an attack, not a counter-method claiming to resist the listed attacks.

relation.reason: Reports how far erased concepts return after parameter-level relearning, measured against erased baselines.

tranche.reason: Text-to-image concept erasure is a new setting, and the paper reports how much comes back after parameter-level relearning. That bears on version B.

source_check.notes: CSR distils from the unerased reference model (the paper calls it 'not an erased-model-only attack'). FLUX strict nudity ends far above the unerased 19.65%, so this shows reactivation, not necessarily retained knowledge. SD nudity values (33-38%) stay below the unerased 52.28%. Ablation numbers are single seed-0 runs and differ from Table 1 (ESD: 32.98 vs 35.79 on SD, 38.25 vs 33.33 on FLUX).

statements.problem: No numbers for this study. Listing SD v1.4/FLUX among non-LLM cases where relearning brings erased content back is accurate (Tables 1-4).
No numbers for this study. 'Weak CSR settings' fits the cited r12: SD-1.4 MACE nudity ASR-Strict 1.75 -> 20.00 vs unerased 52.28 (Table 1; A.6).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CSR on the tested FLUX.1-dev and SD-1.4 erasure/concept settings
reader_labels.reason: CSR raises target-concept recovery measures above erased-model baselines across the reported nudity, violence, artistic-style, entity, abstraction, and relationship settings (r01–r48). The demonstrated recipe uses concept-targeted self-generated anchors and reference-model targets, not unrelated examples or forgotten-fact subsets.
